items.example: Animals in the wild have a huge capacity to adapt to change.
Both natural and man-made factors can lead to the decline of a species.
Destruction of habitat is the main cause of extinction here.
Loss of habitat can occur due to natural disasters or human activities.
Loss of habitat can occur due to natural disasters or climate change.
A whole ecosystem such as a rainforest may be in danger of being lost.
Chemicals can interfere with reproduction, leading to a decline in numbers.
The build-up of chemicals in the environment is dangerous even to large predators.
Large predators feed on smaller animals which have accumulated chemicals.
Some animals are seen as game and hunted for sport.
Grazing animals may stray onto agricultural land in search of food.
The bears stray into villages in search of food.
Large numbers of elephants are killed by poachers each year for their tusks.
If tourism is not regulated, it can have a negative effect on wildlife.
Tourism must be properly regulated to avoid too much disturbance.
Responsible tourism prevents disturbance during the breeding season.
Elephants embark on an annual migration to find water.
It is hard for some animals to reproduce in the wild now.
